impact: Higher-for-longer rates are the main headwind for long-duration growth names like NBIS, BE, PLTR and MU; C benefits from higher short rates. PPI on Friday is the next test.
summary: The 10-year Treasury yield rose more than 7 basis points to about 5.07% on Thursday, the first full session after Veterans Day, and the 2-year climbed more than 11 basis points to about 4.84%. Oil gains and Tuesday's hot October CPI drove the move. Goldman Sachs now expects another quarter-point hike in March, and FedWatch prices a December hike at 100%. Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan said at least two more quarter-point hikes are needed, while Cleveland's Beth Hammack said aggressive increases aren't necessary.
title: 10-year yield jumps to ~5.07%; Goldman adds a March Fed hike
